findings.message: In the unquoted heredoc, `\"` is not an escape sequence, so the generated probe contains `command -v \"jq\"`. Inside `$(...)` the remote sh treats those as literal quote characters and looks up a binary named `"jq"`, quotes included. For every non-wrapper entry (jq, rg, ffmpeg, uv, gh, ...), the probe runs `binary_path="$(command -v \"jq\" || true)"`. That resolves to empty, so the probe prints `missing_binary:jq` and exits 1. Check 3 then always fails with 'Failed to validate runtime binary jq', even on a correctly built image. The sandbox-image check fails the same way.

The list of binaries to verify now comes from the local repo copy `scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json`. The in-image manifest is only checked for existence, so verification no longer reflects what the deployed container or sandbox image was actually built with. verify.sh is run from a checkout whose manifest differs from DEPLOYED_REF, or the sandbox image was built from an older ref. Binaries added in the checkout make a correct deployment fail. Binaries the image actually ships under its own manifest are never checked, so a regression in them passes silently.
